'''Lakeland Square Mall''' is a shopping center situated on the northern side of Lakeland, Florida. Serving Polk County as one of only two enclosed malls, it holds the distinction of being the sole shopping destination off I-4 between Tampa and Orlando. Presently, the mall is anchored by [[Dillard's]], [[Bin Chasers Lakeland]], [[JCPenney|J. C. Penney]], [[Urban Air Adventure Park,]] and [[Cinemark Theatres]].

==History==
Developed by [[Edward J. DeBartolo Jr.|Edward J. DeBartolo]] and [[Homart Development Company|Homart]], Lakeland Square Mall opened in 1988. When it first opened, the mall featured anchor stores such as [[Mervyn's]], [[Sears]], and [[Belk]] (originally signed as Belk-Lindsey), followed shortly by the addition of [[Maison Blanche]], which was originally planned to be [[Robinson's of Florida]], which was acquired by Maison Blanche in 1987. In 1990, [[JCPenney|J. C. Penney]] joined the mall, and in 1994, [[Burdines]] also became part of the lineup, relocating from downtown Lakeland.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.moderncities.com/article/2017-dec-lakeland-two-decades-after-the-road-diets-page-4|title=Lakeland: Two decades after the road diets {{!}} Modern Cities|website=www.moderncities.com|access-date=2019-12-08}}</ref> [[Dillard's]] took over the space previously occupied by [[Mervyn's]] in 1997.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.sun-sentinel.com/news/fl-xpm-1997-01-18-9701170392-story.html|title=MERVYN'S GIVING UP ON FLORIDA|last=Writer|first=DAVID ALTANER Business|website=Sun-Sentinel.com|language=en-US|access-date=2019-12-08}}</ref>

In 1995, General Growth Properties acquired the Homart Company, and management was subsequently transferred to General Growth Properties.

In 1998, [[Maison Blanche]], after being acquired by Dillard's, became Dillard's North, housing the women's departments, while the former Mervyn's location became Dillard's South, housing the men's, children's, and home departements.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.wsj.com/articles/SB895499589971419500|title=Dillard's to Pay $2.9 Billion To Acquire Mercantile Stores|last=Journal|first=Emily Nelson and Robert Berner|date=1998-05-19|work=Wall Street Journal|access-date=2019-12-08|language=en-US|issn=0099-9660}}</ref> In 2004, [[Burdines]] transformed into Burdines-Macy's and completed its transition to [[Macy's]] in 2005. [[Belk]] closed its doors later in the same year, coinciding with the opening of a new Belk location in [[Lakeside Village (Lakeland)|Lakeside Village]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.theledger.com/article/20050702/news/608101810|title=Belk Will Close Its Mall Store|last=Ledger|first=JEREMY MAREADYThe|website=The Ledger|language=en|access-date=2019-12-08}}</ref> The vacant space left by [[Belk]] was filled by a [[Burlington (department store)|Burlington Coat Factory]] in the fall of 2007.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.theledger.com/article/20070404/News/608095204|title=Burlington Coat Factory Coming to Lakeland|last=Ledger|first=JEREMY MAREADYThe|website=The Ledger|language=en|access-date=2019-12-08}}</ref>

[[Dillard's]] South ceased operations in 2012, consolidating its presence to the former [[Maison Blanche]] store.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.theledger.com/article/20120220/News/608112814|title=Dillard's to Close One Of Lakeland Mall Stores|last=KENNEDY|first=KYLE|website=The Ledger|language=en|access-date=2019-12-08}}</ref> The vacant anchor spot once occupied by [[Mervyn's]] was demolished in 2012 to make way for the construction of a new 12-screen [[Cinemark Theatres]] and [[Sports Authority]]. This new complex opened in 2013.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://www.theledger.com/article/20160407/News/811268392|title=Sports Authority location in Lakeland Square Mall set to close|last=report|first=Ledger staff|website=The Ledger|language=en|access-date=2019-12-08}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bizjournals.com/tampabay/blog/morning-edition/2012/05/cinemark-building-12-screen-movie.html|title=Cinemark building 12-screen movie theater in Lakeland|website=www.bizjournals.com|access-date=2019-12-08}}</ref>

In 2015, the [[Sears]] property was among the 235 properties sold by [[Sears Holdings]] to [[Seritage Growth Properties]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.seritage.com/retail/property/3800-us-hwy-98-n/3312500/landing|title=At Lakeland Square | Seritage}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/sears-holdings-completes-seritage-growth-properties-transaction-300109953.html|title=Sears Holdings Completes Seritage Growth Properties Transaction|last=Corporation|first=Sears Holdings|website=www.prnewswire.com|language=en|access-date=2019-12-08}}</ref> [[Sports Authority]] closed along with the rest of the chain in 2016,<ref name=":0" /> and its space was later occupied by Urban Air Adventure Park in August 2018.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.newschief.com/photogallery/LK/20180803/NEWS/803009990/PH/1|title=Photos: Urban Air Adventure Park opens in North Lakeland|website=News Chief|language=en|access-date=2019-12-08}}</ref> [[Macy's]] closed in 2017, and [[Resale America]] took over the space in November 2019.<ref>{{Citation|title=Re-Sale America Lakeland Grand Opening 2019|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=O0oHhiaQp_g|language=en|access-date=2019-12-08}}</ref>

[[Sears]], as part of a 142-store closure round, also closed in 2018.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.theledger.com/news/20181016/lakeland-sears-part-of-corporate-shutdowns|title=Lakeland Sears part of corporate shutdowns|last=Pera|first=Eric|website=The Ledger|language=en|access-date=2019-12-08}}</ref> [[Charlotte Russe (retailer)|Charlotte Russe]], which had closed earlier in the year, reopened at the mall as part of the chain's plan to open 100 stores in 2019.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/charlotte-russe-retail-locations-relaunched-300862601.html|title=Charlotte Russe Retail Locations Relaunched|last=Inc|first=Y. M.|website=www.prnewswire.com|language=en|access-date=2019-12-08}}</ref> In 2022, [[Burlington (department store)|Burlington]] closed its doors and relocated across the street to the Shoppes of Lakeland shopping center.

In 2026, [[Rural King]] filed plans to open a store in the {{Convert|151,276|sqft|m2|adj=on}} building that was formerly Sears.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-09-24 |title=Rural King eyes new Lakeland store. Here's what we know |url=https://www.yahoo.com/news/articles/rural-king-eyes-lakeland-store-173141691.html |access-date=2026-11-05 |website=Yahoo News |language=en-US}}</ref>
